# Analyses of runs 1 and 2 (generated by scripts/analyze.py)

Run 1 (`results/run1_preregistered_only/`) is the preregistered run. Run 2 (`results/run2/`) re-runs the same pipeline with the same seed and adds a post-hoc test set with unseen phrasings and a post-hoc over-masking metric. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over test tickets (1,000 resamples); differences between strategies or test sets are paired by ticket/author. Register of 5,000 people unless stated.

## 1. Reproducibility of run 1 inside run 2

*Verification, not an analysis: run 2 regenerated the data and re-ran every preregistered measurement on the original test set.*

Data file hashes (`data/manifest.json`): train `cf133f34e23e…`, test `3697b570bf26…`, shifted `2af3ceb47516…`.

| Strategy | Largest absolute difference of any preregistered point estimate (run 2 − run 1) | Share of tickets with identical per-ticket attack outcome |

| S1_regex | 0.0000 | 1.000 |
| S2_ner | 0.0000 | 1.000 |

## 2. Protocol hypotheses H1–H4 (run 1)

*H1–H4 are recorded in the protocol. The decision rules in this table were operationalized after run 1.*

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | supported | S4 linkage top-1 = 0.429 [0.402, 0.458]; rule: lower bound > 0.20. |
| H2 | supported | S2 − S3 linkage top-1 = 0.279 [0.254, 0.305] (paired); rule: lower bound > 0. S3 was tested on the phrasings it was trained on; on unseen phrasings (post-hoc) the difference is 0.275 [0.248, 0.304]. |
| H3 | first part not testable (U1 at ceiling); second part supported | U1 macro-F1 = 1.000–1.000 for every strategy, so the comparison 'reduces re-identification more than U1' is trivially true and uninformative (relative re-identification reduction vs. S0: S5 78.0%, S6 98.5%; U1 reduction 0). U2 = 1.000 for every strategy. |
| H4 | supported | rule: point estimates strictly decrease 1k → 5k → 20k and the paired 1k − 20k difference excludes 0. Met by every strategy; for S3 the effect is at the floor (≤ 0.001 at every size). |

Character-level precision of S3's predicted spans (share of masked non-space characters that are identity characters): original 1.000, shifted 0.933.

Most frequent S3 predicted spans on the shifted set that are not entirely inside a gold identity span ('<name> writing' = the name masked together with the following word): '<name> writing' (195), '12' (111), 'trade' (85), 'door' (16), 'green door' (2). The house number in 'the <occupation> at number 12' is a literal of the template and therefore not annotated as identity; masking it is arguably correct and is a limitation of the annotation scheme, not of the detector. 'trade' ('by trade') and 'door' ('the green door') are genuine over-masking.

## 6. Privacy–utility trade-off (run 2)

*Post-hoc summary. Re-identification and semantic similarity are preregistered measures; 'other words kept' (share of non-identity words still present, a direct measure of over-masking) is post-hoc. On the original phrasings no strategy deletes non-identity words, so 'other words kept' is 1.000 everywhere and cannot rank strategies; the trade-off is summarized with semantic similarity: the Spearman rank correlation between linkage top-1 and semantic similarity across the seven strategies (+1 means that every gain in privacy is paid for in similarity, in the same order). Semantic similarity also falls when identity spans are removed, which is the intended effect, so it mixes privacy gain with utility loss; 'other words kept' isolates the loss of non-identity content.*


**Original test set** — strategies from most to least re-identifiable: S0 > S1 > S4 > S2 > S5 > S6 > S3; Spearman ρ(linkage top-1, semantic similarity) = 1.00.

| S1_regex | 0.712 [0.684, 0.740] | 0.096 [0.076, 0.117] | 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] | 0.985 [0.983, 0.987] |

## 7. Phrasing × values: is S3 memorizing the attribute values? (probe)

*Post-hoc probe (`scripts/probe_unseen_values.py`, results in `results/probe_unseen_values/`). Run 2's shifted set changes phrasing but reuses the closed vocabulary of values seen in training. The probe draws a new population whose names, towns, occupations, employers, clubs and streets are all new, and applies the run-2 S3 model without retraining. Ages, arrival years and club roles keep their original ranges.*

The value-memorization explanation is not supported: with new values and the original phrasings S3 keeps the same near-zero re-identification. What degrades is phrasing: with unseen phrasings S3 misses about half of the ages (see section 4), whether or not the values are new.
